This is an RCT comparing two different fentanyl infusion techniques (continuous vs bolus) combined with ketamine and droperidol for total intravenous anesthesia. It explicitly measures explicit memory and dreams during anesthesia, which relates to awareness. Meets criteria as an RCT of anaesthetic regimens.

This is a prospective observational study analyzing pharmacodynamic interactions using a response surface model, not a randomized controlled trial. No randomization to different interventions is described.

This is an observational study investigating EEG and AEP parameters to detect consciousness transitions. Patients received remifentanil with either sevoflurane or propofol, but there was no randomization to different anaesthetic interventions. The study focuses on monitoring techniques rather than testing anaesthetic regimens or monitors as interventions.
This study explicitly uses 'nine healthy volunteers' rather than surgical patients. The selection criteria explicitly exclude volunteer studies.

This is an RCT comparing BIS-guided isoflurane titration versus standard clinical practice without BIS monitoring. It tests an anaesthetic depth monitor (BIS) as an intervention, which is explicitly included in the selection criteria.

While this is an RCT, it tests esmolol and nicardipine for maintaining hemodynamic stability, not anaesthetic regimens or depth monitors for preventing awareness. The primary outcomes are hemodynamic responses and recovery profile, not awareness or anaesthetic depth for unconsciousness.
This is a large observational multicenter study reporting the incidence of awareness (19,575 patients). It is not a randomized controlled trial testing any anaesthetic intervention.
This is an RCT comparing two different anaesthetic regimens (propofol-remifentanil vs sevoflurane-N2O) for day case surgery. It meets the criteria as an RCT of anaesthetic regimens.

This is an RCT comparing closed-loop automated BIS-guided propofol titration versus manual BIS-guided control. It tests an anaesthetic depth monitor (BIS) intervention for maintaining unconsciousness, meeting the inclusion criteria.
This is an RCT comparing etomidate versus thiopentone sodium as induction agents. It tests anaesthetic drug regimens (induction), which meets the inclusion criteria.
This is a software/methodology paper describing the metafor R package for conducting meta-analyses. It is not a clinical study of anaesthetic interventions.

This is a comparative method study evaluating two monitors (Narcotrend vs BIS) in the same 50 patients. It is not a randomized controlled trial randomizing patients to different interventions; both monitors were used simultaneously on all patients.

This is an RCT comparing different anaesthetic regimens (remifentanil+desflurane/sevoflurane vs alfentanil+desflurane). The abstract explicitly mentions 'No awareness occurred', indicating awareness was considered. Meets criteria as an RCT of anaesthetic regimens.

This is an RCT with six groups comparing different anaesthetic techniques (varying MAC levels of isoflurane, with/without fentanyl, with/without lidocaine).
